svg.title: You write down what should be true
svg.desc: A six-step numbered chain from kubectl apply through the API server into etcd, out to the controllers and scheduler and down to the kubelet, with a struck-out ssh-and-docker-run shortcut beside it, next to a large dashed reconciliation loop whose four stations are desired state, observe actual, diff and act; below, an honest four-row decision table ending in Kubernetes only for many services across many teams, and five broken-pod boxes labelled ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled, CrashLoopBackOff, CreateContainerConfigError and Pending Insufficient cpu.
svg.text: You write down what should be true
scheduler writes nodeName back into etcd
kubelet on node-2 -> containerd -> your pod
kubectl NEVER talks to a node. It
writes a record, and six controllers
race to make the record true.
forever, every few seconds, for every object
and should you actually use it?
K8s costs about 0.5 FTE to run. That is the
number nobody puts in the proposal.
and the five you will actually see
...and what keeps traffic off a pod that is not ready? -> M2
